- We need explicit assignment of output ownership to Arcadia for any user-generated content.

Would appreciate a quick call to align before legal escalation.

Subject: Fwd: Arcadia MSA redlines re: output / retrain / feedback license

Laura / Marissa — forwarding redlines from Arcadia. Key commercial asks summarized below. Can legal propose language we can send back that balances Arcadia's concerns with Redwood's need to continue improving models?

Summary of their asks:
- Output ownership: Arcadia wants assignment (they wrote "all customer-generated output shall be the sole property of Arcadia").
- Retrain prohibition: no training or model re-use on customer content without separate written consent.
- Feedback license: limited metrics-only license, opt-in for anything that includes PII.

My read: we rarely assign title to outputs (we typically grant customers broad usage rights and an output license). For retraining, we already exclude customer-specific fine-tuning without opt-in, but the MSA redline language is broader than our current feedback license. Proposed path: engage on a compromise that (a) grants a strong customer usage right to outputs, (b) disallows automatic inclusion in model retraining unless explicitly opted into and with de-identification guarantees, and (c) offers a limited telemetry license for product improvement (aggregate metrics + synthetic training data allowed under strict controls).

Can you draft proposed redlines we can send to Sophie by EOD Friday? If there are material legal concessions we shouldn't grant, flag them and I'll escalate. I can schedule a short sync with Arcadia if helpful.

Thanks — Jonas

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Arcadia MSA redlines re: output / retrain / feedback license

Jonas / Marissa — reviewed Arcadia's redlines. Below are suggested counter-provisions and rationale. Happy to put them into tracked changes for the MSA.

1) Customer rights to output
- Suggested language: "Customer shall own the outputs generated by Customer prompts and interactions (\"Customer Outputs\"). Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive right to use, reproduce, and distribute Customer Outputs. Redwood retains no ownership of Customer Outputs."
- Rationale: This addresses Arcadia's ask on title without creating a carveout that would prevent Redwood from using de-identified aggregates for product improvement.

2) Training / retraining on customer content
- Suggested language: "Redwood shall not use Customer data or Customer Outputs to train or further develop Redwood's underlying models without Customer's prior written consent. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry and system metrics for service improvement and research, provided such data cannot be reverse-engineered to re-identify Customer or End Users."
- Rationale: Strong protection for Arcadia while preserving our ability to continue using non-identifiable aggregates. Note: 'de-identified' needs definitional detail (we should propose a short definition in the MSA).

3) Feedback license and telemetry
- Suggested language: "Customer grants Redwood a limited, revocable, non-exclusive license to use system telemetry and aggregated, de-identified usage metrics solely to operate and improve the Redwood Service. Redwood will not use PII or identifiable Customer Content for model training absent explicit Customer opt-in."
- Rationale: Keeps telemetry narrow and reversible. For customers who want upgrades in exchange for broader usage rights, we can negotiate separate data programs (with compensation).

4) Audit / SOC2 / retention
- Proposal: provide SOC 2 Type II attestation, details on retention windows, and sample audit logs. For anything beyond standard artifacts, require an NDA plus commercial consideration.

Next steps: I will generate tracked-change redlines for the MSA/Order Form with the exact clauses (including a precise de-identification definition and an opt-in flow). If Arcadia insists on full assignment language we should push for the usage-right formulation above; assignment can have unintended consequences (e.g., customer claiming copyright in model-generated system prompts).

I'll aim to have marked-up documents by Thu EOD. If you plan to call Arcadia before that, let me know and I can join.

— Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Arcadia MSA redlines re: output / retrain / feedback license

Sophie — thanks for the clear redlines and patience while we pulled legal in. Attached is a proposed counter (tracked changes) that implements the compromise below.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Customer Outputs: Redwood will concede that Customer "owns" Customer Outputs; we will add a definition for Customer Outputs and grant Arcadia a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive right to use, reproduce, and distribute those outputs.
- Retraining / model usage: Redwood will not use Customer data or Customer Outputs to train or fine-tune Redwood's underlying base or backbone models without Arcadia's prior written consent.
- Limited telemetry license: Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and system metrics for service improvement and diagnostics. Redwood will not use PII or identifiable Customer Content for model training without explicit opt-in and documented de-identification processes.
- Option for a separate data program: If Arcadia wants broader model-access / research participation (e.g., to accelerate product integrations), we can negotiate a separate compensated data program with tighter controls and a versioned consent flow.

We also included a proposed de-identification definition and an audit commitment: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II and sample retention/audit log documentation; any deeper forensic access would be scoped under an NDA and reasonable cost recovery.

Next steps: I've attached the redlines (Arcadia_MSA_redline_v3.docx) with our tracked changes. Could you confirm if this captures your priorities and whether procurement needs anything else to move the PO? Happy to hop on a 20-minute call to close open items.

Best,
